headline: Ansar Allah parliament speaker Yahya al-Rai warns Cairo against military intervention in Yemen
dek: Yahya al-Rai, head of the Ansar Allah-affiliated legislature in Sanaa, sent an 'urgent message' to Egyptian parliament speaker Hisham Badawi ahead of the emergency session: 'We categorically reject dragging Egypt... into a war that is in no way compatible with its own values' and said Sanaa follows…
sources: Ansar Allah-affiliated SABA news agency via Turkiye Today/EuropeSays; The National
fault_line: Is an Egyptian deployment a protector-of-the-holy-sites move — or a repeat of the 1960s Yemen 'graveyard' trap?

sections.what_happened: Yahya al-Rai, head of the Ansar Allah-affiliated legislature in Sanaa, sent an 'urgent message' to Egyptian parliament speaker Hisham Badawi ahead of the emergency session: 'We categorically reject dragging Egypt... into a war that is in no way compatible with its own values' and said Sanaa follows 'with great concern any inclination that could lead Egypt to take part in military moves serving the policies of the Saudi regime in Yemen.'
sections.what_verified: The National independently reports the warning; Turkiye Today/EuropeSays cite SABA. No wire (Reuters/AP) pick-up yet of the al-Rai message specifically.
sections.what_disputed: Single attributed source chain (SABA → aggregators) for the exact quotes; no independent confirmation of the message's delivery.
sections.why_matters: The Ansar Allah side draws a red line at Cairo: while Egypt's parliament sits in closed session, Sanaa is publicly warning Egyptians not to repeat the 1960s Yemen intervention. Pocketbook hook: Suez already lost ~$11bn since 2023 (Egyptian FM, via Dawn) — the real reason Cairo cannot stay out. Pair with 1400-01/1400-02 context.
